title: gpu-nsight-occupancy-analysis-2026-03-22
content:
Summary:

This note collects Nsight investigation results for GPU utilization and occupancy across a number of recent inference runs. Goal was to understand low SM utilization observed in p99 latency workloads for short sequence generation (seq_len 8-64) and identify actionable fixes: better kernel fusion, CUDA Graph capture points, or batching strategy changes.

Test bed / configuration:
- Host: rtx-serve-03 (internal lab)
- GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.2)
- Runtime: redwood-serving v0.9.13 (inference-engine + CUDA graph wrappers)
- Model: open-llm/gpt-3-medium-ish (decoder-only, 24 layers, hidden=2048) — using quantized int8 kernels for GEMM where applicable
- Typical request shapes: batch sizes 1-8 (most p99 issues at bs=1, bs=2), seq lengths 8 / 16 / 32
- Capture configs: Nsight Systems 2026.1 captures; timeline + CUDA kernel sampling + API trace; separate Nsight Compute on hot kernels (fused_attention, matmul_gemm, softmax, layernorm)

What we observed (high level):
- End-to-end GPU utilization (SM % active) during single-request runs is low: 10-30% on average for seq_len <= 32, bursts up to 60% during matmul heavy windows.
- Achieved occupancy for several small kernels is very low (10-25% of theoretical) shown in Nsight Compute profiles: low active warps and poor register/block utilization.
- Kernel launch overheads and host->device synchronization points are frequent when CUDA Graph capture is not used; these manifest as white gaps in the kernel timeline and many short kernels grouped together.
- Long-running GEMM kernels (cublas + custom int8 GEMM) reach high SM utilization and close to expected throughput, but they are intermittent.
- Fused attention kernels (custom fused_fwd_attention) show moderate utilization but are memory-bound on keys/vals scatter and softmax steps.

Detailed timeline notes (Nsight Systems captures):
- Capture: nsight-capture-bs1-s8-2026-03-18.nsys
  - Timeline shows: small sequence of tiny kernels per layer: token-embedding lookup (small memcpy), layernorm, attention_fwd (split into 3 kernels: qkv linear, scaled-dot-prod, softmax), matmul for output projection, kv cache write.
  - There are ~48 kernel launches per layer for our implementation variant (unfused ops). Each launch is sub-200us for many kernels; cumulative kernel time small but host overhead dominates.
  - Frequent cudaStreamSynchronize calls placed in the code path for correctness checks appear to serialize execution and cause low overlap.

- Capture: nsight-capture-cudagraphs-bs1-s8-2026-03-19.nsys
  - With CUDA Graphs enabled and capture point around the entire forward pass per-token, kernel launch overheads are eliminated and kernels appear as a single CUDA graph instantiation hot path. SM utilization increases ~1.8x (from ~20% to ~36%) for same shape.
  - However, not all kernels are incorporated into the graph due to dynamic shape branches (position-dependent ops) — these residual small kernels still break overlap.

- Nsight Compute profile: fused_attention_fwd (hot)
  - Achieved occupancy: 28% (SMs active: 56/108), theoretical occupancy limited by register usage per thread; register spills minimal.
  - Memory throughput: 40% of peak HBM bandwidth — indicates memory-bound for some attention scatter/gather and softmax.
  - Warp efficiency: 88% (not terrible), but divergence spikes on small batch sizes due to masked softmax lanes.

- Nsight Compute profile: small-kernel-layernorm / rmsnorm kernels
  - These tiny kernels show occupancy ~12-18% and high per-thread register utilization limiting block size.
  - Many launches are <50us — launch overhead becomes a dominant fraction.

Root causes (hypothesis backed by captures):
1) Kernel fragmentation: many small unfused kernels (layernorm, bias-add, slice, reshape) per layer cause frequent kernel launches and poor occupancy. Host overhead and scheduling reduces overlap.
2) Low arithmetic intensity on certain kernels (softmax, KV scatter) -> memory-bandwidth limited, so high SM occupancy doesn't translate to higher throughput.
3) Register pressure in fused kernels reduces achievable occupancy; tuning launch configuration / reducing per-thread register usage could allow larger thread blocks and higher occupancy.
4) Incomplete CUDA Graph capture: dynamic branches and per-token branching prevented full capture; our fallback path uses host launches.

Actionable recommendations / experiments:
- Short term (quick wins):
  - Enable full-graph capture for the common path: add a preprocessing normalization that makes per-layer shapes deterministic during capture. Try capture at granularity: whole-token-forward (works well) vs per-layer graphs.
  - Remove gratuitous cudaStreamSynchronize and correctness-check synchronizations on p99 path; replace with asynchronous checks or gated debug builds. (PR: GH repo/inference-runtime#PR-412)
  - Batch small ops into composite kernels: fuse layernorm + bias-add + gelu where possible (microfusion). This reduces launches and increases arithmetic intensity.

- Mid term (engineering work):
  - Rework attention implementation: shift some scatter/gather to tiled shared-memory flows to increase data reuse and reduce global memory traffic for small seq lengths. Measure HBM BW usage before/after.
  - Tune kernel launch params (blockDim/gridDim) and compile flags to reduce register usage for fused_attention to raise occupancy from 28% -> target 40-50%. Try nvcc flags: --maxrregcount=64 as an experiment and measure spill tradeoffs.
  - Expand CUDA Graph coverage with multi-path capture: record multiple graphs for different token-length buckets and dispatch appropriate graph at runtime. This avoids dynamic branching at capture time.

- Long term / research:
  - Investigate dynamic kernel batching across concurrent user requests to increase amortized occupancy for small requests without increasing p50 latency (scheduling window).
  - Evaluate static kernel-codegen with Triton-like approach for per-model/per-shape specialized kernels; may increase maintenance cost but yields much higher utilization for small seqs.

Measured improvements from quick experiments:
- After removing syncs and enabling per-token CUDA graph capture for common path: average SM utilization for bs=1,s8 increased from 18% -> 34%. p99 latency improved ~12% (due to less idle CPU blocking).
- Fusing layernorm+bias-add reduced number of kernel launches per layer from ~48 -> ~35 and reduced cumulative kernel launch overhead by ~30% in captures.

Open questions / next steps:
- Need to quantify softmax memory-bound portion vs compute-bound: run Nsight Compute with targeted memory roofline analysis on softmax and attention scatter.
- Test --maxrregcount experiments for fused_attention on CI GPU (A100) to ensure spills don't negate occupancy gains.
- Implement multi-bucket CUDA Graph capture and measure complexity/perf tradeoff.
- Coordinate with release-engineering to run experiments on Dedicated hardware types (A10/A100 L4) to get representative profiles.

Appendix: useful captures / artifacts (links referenced in linked_artifacts):
- nsight captures: nsight-capture-bs1-s8-2026-03-18.nsys, nsight-capture-cudagraphs-bs1-s8-2026-03-19.nsys
- PR: GH repo/inference-runtime#PR-412 (remove syncs + add graph capture config)
- Jira: INF-879 (investigate low p99 utilization for short sequences)

Notes to self / rough todos (scratch):
- add automated nsight capture job in perf CI for shapes: [(bs1,s8),(bs1,s32),(bs4,s16)]
- run nvprof/ncu on L4 to compare behavior (L4 poor HBM -> will highlight memory issues)
- try capture with entirely static dispatch (no branches) and compare perf/compilation size

If reviewers want, I can attach the raw nsys captures to the JIRA ticket.

-- Aisha
